Design notes / deviation from the literal .cpp+.hpp+_fi.F90 triad, and why:
- Modules_Interface.f90 was not a Fortran module (no module/end module) — it was two plain subroutines, each already declared `bind(C, name="modules_fi_init_"/"modules_fi_finalize_")`. The sole external caller is software/mcfm/src/BLHA/CXX_Interface.cxx (a shared file, out of scope for this unit), which itself declares `extern "C" { void modules_fi_init_(); void modules_fi_finalize_(); }` and calls them directly — no Fortran code calls these by their plain names.
- Because the original bind(C) name IS the external symbol CXX_Interface.cxx expects, a Fortran `_fi.F90` shim re-declaring `bind(C, name="modules_fi_init_")` would define the same linker symbol a second time (duplicate symbol vs. the C++ definition) — so no Fortran shim was created. This is called out in a comment in the .cpp.
- The two subroutines only orchestrate calling `<mod>_init()`/`<mod>_finalize()` for all 58 already-translated Mods/*_mod modules (ewcharge_mod, zcouple_mod, b0_mod, ... msq_struc_mod) in the source's exact order — verified module-by-module that each defines a public `<mod>_init`/`<mod>_finalize` subroutine inside `module <mod> ... end module`. Those remain genuine Fortran symbols (no C++ equivalent exists — the C++ side only exposes raw data accessors), so per the Spec's "callee is still Fortran → declare the plain Fortran symbol in extern C" rule, each is declared via its real gfortran-mangled name `__<mod>_MOD_<mod>_init/_finalize` (all lowercase). All 58 init manglings were cross-checked byte-for-byte against the ground-truth list in software/pepper/src/mcfm_analytics/validators/mod_inits_arr.h (exact match); finalize manglings follow the identical, standard gfortran convention (no finalize ground-truth file exists, but the pattern is mechanical and confirmed via each module's own source declaring `<mod>_finalize` public inside the same `module <mod>`). Call order for both init and finalize was diffed 1:1 against the original file's `call` statements — identical.
- Left the shared CMakeLists.txt untouched per hard constraints (Integrate step wires it in); did not build or run tests.
- Also spotted (not touched, out of scope): software/mcfm/src/Mods/b0_mod.f90 and several sibling _mod.f90 shims in this same folder still carry leftover "LLM INSTRUCTIONS" prompt-style comment blocks from a prior translation pass — pre-existing, unrelated to this unit, flagging for awareness only.

Notable design decision, flagged for the human reviewer / Integrate: this is the *only* file in the whole mcfm-translate tree with a `character*(*)` dummy argument — there was zero existing precedent for a Fortran string across this extern-C boundary anywhere in the codebase. I used the standard Fortran-2003 interop idiom instead of guessing at gfortran's hidden-length ABI: the `_fi.F90` shim's bind(C) interface declares `character(kind=c_char), dimension(*)` and the call site passes `trim(label)//c_null_char`, so the C++ wrapper just takes a plain null-terminated `const char*`. This sidesteps needing to invent a hidden-length-argument convention. All 6 real call sites pass exact-length string literals (checked via grep across every caller of `ggZZcapture` in the tree), so trim(label) is a no-op for every exercised path and the translation is behavior-preserving beyond a reasonable doubt — not just on the happy path.
